correctness.rationale: For iid uniform eccentric anomalies on a noncircular ellipse, equal-distance circumcenter equations imply Z=(z1+z2+z3+(z1 z2 z3)^(-1))/4. The linear integer torus homomorphism (u,v,w)->(u+v,u-v,-u+w) is onto Haar, producing X=cos(u)(cos(v)+cos(w))/2 and Y=sin(u)(cos(v)-cos(w))/2. Inverting the two independent arcsine variables yields the given a.e. normalized density with correct Jacobian |cosu sinu|/2 and filled astroid support. Fourier phase balance yields mixed moments with p-q divisible by four; independent exact E Z^4=3/32 and E|Z|^4=7/64. Unique right-cusp preimage at all zero angles; Taylor expansion 1-X=(sum theta_i^2+S^2)/8+O(|theta|^4), Y=(S^3-sum theta_i^3)/24+O(|theta|^5) and det(I+11^T)=4 give cusp probability 4sqrt2/(3 pi^2)*t^(3/2), uniform ellipsoid angle law in total variation, and weak 2D mark limit. Independent exact coefficients checked. The proof is local analytic with full dimensional integration; finite Monte Carlo alone cannot prove cusp asymptotics.
